subject: Network onramp options for HarborLogix private deployment

Subject: Network onramp options for HarborLogix private deployment

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We’re moving toward a private deployment of Redwood in our AWS accounts and need help picking the right onramp pattern: VPC peering, PrivateLink (interface endpoints), or a site-to-site (S2S) VPN (or a hybrid of those). A couple of constraints to consider:

- Multi-account, multi-region setup (US-EAST-1 primary, US-WEST-2 DR)
- Latency-sensitive inference traffic (P99 under 120ms) for a small subset of calls
- Strong egress control and least public exposure for data inferences (SOC 2 in scope)
- We aim for a low-ops PoC in 2-3 weeks and a production rollout in ~2 months

Can you summarize trade-offs and what you’d recommend for a PoC vs production? Also, any templates/diagram stubs you can share would be helpful.

Thanks,
Nathan Park
Head of Infrastructure, HarborLogix
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Network onramp options for HarborLogix private deployment

Hi Nathan — great to meet yesterday. High level guidance below; I’ve attached a short connectivity matrix (connectivity-matrix-v1.pdf) you can use for the PoC decision. Happy to run a quick 30m workshop to map this to your topology.

Short recommendation summary:
- PrivateLink (interface endpoints) — recommended for production when you need per-service private endpoints, fine-grained control, and minimal cross-account routing. Pros: scoped access, no route table changes across accounts, easy to audit. Cons: slightly higher per-GB cost and more endpoint ENIs to manage across regions.
- VPC Peering — good for high-throughput, low-latency paths when accounts can accept full-route visibility. Pros: lower egress cost in some clouds and simple L3 connectivity. Cons: doesn’t support transitive peering; scales poorly with many accounts/regions and is harder to centralize.
- Site-to-site VPN — fastest to stand up for PoC across on-prem or when using transit gateway later. Pros: quick, can be encrypted over internet, minimal infra changes. Cons: higher latencies/less predictable performance, operational burden for long term unless replaced by PrivateLink or Transit-based designs.

Suggested path for your timeline:
1) PoC (2–3 weeks): stand up an S2S VPN to Redwood Private control plane endpoints in US-EAST-1 for functional validation and compliance checks. This minimizes infra work and lets SREs exercise auth, logging, and traffic patterns.
2) Pilot (4–6 weeks): If PoC looks good, iterate on PrivateLink in US-EAST-1 for low-latency calls and use a regional peering/transit for bulk/batch traffic if needed.
3) Production (target ~2 months): Migrate latency-critical endpoints to PrivateLink with per-region endpoints, use Transit Gateway or central peering fabric for cross-region replication/backup.

Questions for sizing and final recommendation:
- Expected qps and average request size for inference calls (tokens/KB)
- Do you control both VPCs/accounts or do we need cross-account setup with your security team?
- Any mandatory cloud vendor constraints (only AWS, or mixed cloud)?

I attached a matrix and a short checklist. If you want I can loop in Lauren with an architecture note and Ben on an ops checklist.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra

Hi Nathan — quick commercial note to align on the PoC/production path Rishi outlined. For the PoC (VPN-based) there is no platform charge beyond standard usage; when you move to PrivateLink we typically account for interface endpoint egress in the usage forecasts. If you prefer, we can create a short-term pilot pricing SKU to cover any unexpected egress while we validate latency/SLA.

If you’re comfortable with that approach, I’ll draft a 60-day pilot amendment to the MSA and include a rollback clause (we expect most customers to migrate to PrivateLink for prod to reduce operational overhead). Ben — can you confirm the standard network checklist we share with customers is up-to-date for PrivateLink guidance?

—Marissa Cole

Thanks — that sounds like a good plan. A few quick answers to your questions:
- Expected peak: ~400 qps, mostly short requests (payloads ~2–5KB), long tail at night for batch ops
- Accounts: We control app and infra accounts in AWS (cross-account setup is fine)
- Cloud: AWS-only for the initial rollout (we may add Azure later)

I’ve uploaded our current topology sketch (harbor-topology-v2.drawio) to the Drive link below and can schedule a 30m workshop tomorrow at 10:30am PT. That time works for our networking/infra leads.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/harborlogix/designs/harbor-topology-v2

Nathan — thanks for the details and the topology link. A couple of operational items ahead of the workshop:

- Confirm preferred maintenance window for routing changes (we’ll need one brief window if we test peering or endpoint attachment)
- For PrivateLink we recommend mutual TLS to the endpoint and per-endpoint Security Group locking; please share the security group baseline you want enforced.
- For the PoC VPN please provide the customer edge IPs and IKE parameters so our SREs can pre-configure tunnels.

I’ve attached a short ops checklist (included in connectivity-matrix-v1.pdf) — we’ll walk through it in the call. Looking forward to the workshop.

—Ben Carter
Solution Architect, Redwood Inference
